title: Giant Effective Permeability in Drude Thin Films Probed by THz Time-Domain Spectroscopy
authors: Gian Paolo Papari, Zahra Mazaheri, Antonio Vettoliere, Carmine Granata, Roberto Russo, Giovanni Ausanio, Umar Farooq, Junaid Yaseen, Can Koral, Antonello Andreone
abstract: The electromagnetic response of metallic films is commonly analyzed in terahertz spectroscopy by assuming unit relative magnetic permeability. In this work we show that this assumption introduces significant distortions in the electrodynamic retrieval of highly conductive films. Aluminum and copper films, 10 nm thick, were investigated by terahertz time-domain spectroscopy in both transmission and reflection configurations. By applying a self consistent retrieval method that independently determines the complex permittivity and permeability, we show that the Drude-type dielectric response is systematically accompanied by a permeability that strongly departs from unity. This deviation is intrinsically linked to the reactive impedance of the films, which clarifies the light induced onset of large screening currents within a transversally confined geometry. A phenomenological interpretation based on the Faraday Neumann Lenz mechanism and a lumped-element model of the film impedance accounts for the observed trends. These results indicate that the common assumption $\tildeμ=1$ in non-magnetic Drude films can lead to an incomplete or biased electrodynamic characterization in the terahertz regime.
summary: This work demonstrates that assuming unit magnetic permeability ($\mu=1$) when analyzing THz spectroscopy data for metals like Al and Cu leads to inaccurate electrodynamic characterization. By employing a self-consistent retrieval method, the authors show that the effective permeability significantly deviates from unity due to large screening currents induced by time-varying magnetic fields. This highlights the necessity of treating $	ilde{\mu}$ as an independent variable in such analyses.
main_problem: The standard assumption of unit relative magnetic permeability (mu=1) when analyzing THz spectroscopy data for metallic films introduces significant errors in retrieving the true electrodynamic parameters.
main_result: The effective permeability ($	ilde{\mu}$) significantly deviates from unity, a deviation attributed not to intrinsic magnetism but to macroscopic screening currents governed by the Faraday-Neumann-Lenz effect.
method: The authors employed a self-consistent retrieval method (CTVT) on both transmission and reflection THz time-domain spectroscopy data to independently determine complex permittivity ($	ilde{\epsilon}$) and permeability ($	ilde{\mu}$).
model_or_system: The study investigates highly conductive thin films of Aluminum and Copper deposited on substrates, analyzing their response in the terahertz frequency range using Drude dielectric modeling.
key_observables: Complex permittivity ($	ilde{\epsilon}$), complex permeability ($	ilde{\mu}$), complex refractive index ($	ilde{n}$), and normalized impedance ($	ilde{z}$).
important_parameters: Plasma frequency ($\omega_p$), relaxation time ($\omega_	au$), skin depth ($\delta(\omega)$), and the ratio of THz wavelength to skin depth ($\lambda_{in} / \delta$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption challenged is $	ilde{\mu}=1$; the analysis requires treating $	ilde{\epsilon}$ and $	ilde{\mu}$ independently for accurate characterization.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate time-dependent THz signals, polar representations of electrodynamic parameters showing phase constraints, and comparisons of skin depths calculated under different assumptions ($	ilde{\mu}=1$ vs. free retrieval).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem with $	ilde{\mu}=1$, details the self-consistent retrieval methodology using THz-TDS data for Al/Cu films, presents results showing large deviations in $	ilde{\mu}$, and finally provides a physical interpretation linking this deviation to screening currents via the FNL effect.
why_interesting: While focused on classical electromagnetism, the concept of induced macroscopic fields (screening currents) leading to parameter misinterpretation mirrors how boundary conditions or approximations can fundamentally alter the perceived quantum state or response in complex open quantum systems.
